title: API 580 Training in Denver: Risk Based Inspection Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 580 exam prep for Denver RBI planners, integrity engineers and inspectors: refinery and gas plant programmes, PSM, RP 580 4th edition.
h1: API 580 Training in Denver: Risk-Based Inspection Exam Prep for Inspection Planners, Integrity Engineers and Inspectors
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection work around Denver

Denver has more integrity engineers than its single refinery would suggest. Operators, midstream companies and consultants run DJ Basin and Rocky Mountain programmes from offices in and around the city, and the inspection planners at Suncor's Commerce City refinery and at Weld County gas plants face the questions RBI is designed to answer: which equipment carries the risk, what the data really says, and how far an inspection plan can be justified before someone asks for proof. API 580 certifies knowledge of that discipline as API RP 580 describes it.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Denver. The API 580 course is self-paced and online, and an instructor answers your questions as you work through RP 580. The American Petroleum Institute sets the eligibility rules, administers the examination and certifies those who pass, and its programme page says the exam can be scheduled at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring. For a planner who spends half the week at field locations, being able to sit the exam without a trip to a test centre may decide the timing.

Who sits API 580 in Denver

Holders of a current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certificate qualify automatically, so many candidates are inspectors who want the risk side of the job on paper. Others qualify through education and petrochemical industry experience: an engineering degree with one year, a two-year degree with two years, a high school diploma with three, or five years with no formal education. Around Denver that second group tends to include:

  • inspection planners and reliability engineers at the Commerce City refinery and its contractors, who build or maintain inspection plans and want to understand how risk-based plans are justified;
  • integrity engineers at operators and midstream companies with Colorado offices, such as Chevron, which runs its Colorado business from a regional headquarters in Denver, and SM Energy, headquartered in Denver, which completed its merger with Civitas Resources in 2026;
  • corrosion and materials specialists, including graduates of Colorado School of Mines' metallurgical and materials engineering programme, who lead damage mechanism reviews;
  • consultants who run RBI studies for owners across the Rockies and need a recognised credential to show for it.

Whether upstream production experience counts as petrochemical industry experience is a question for API, not for this page. Describe the facilities and the work accurately on the application.

PSM mechanical integrity in Adams and Weld counties

Colorado has no OSHA-approved State Plan for private employers, so federal OSHA enforces process safety management at private sites. OSHA's Denver Area Office covers Adams, Denver and Weld counties, along with Boulder, Larimer and much of northern and western Colorado; the Englewood Area Office covers the rest of the state. Under 29 CFR 1910.119(j), the mechanical integrity element applies to pressure vessels and storage tanks, piping systems, relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, controls and pumps. Inspection and testing procedures must follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, and their frequency must be consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice, increasing where operating experience shows the need.

The standard does not require RBI. What it requires is a defensible frequency, and RBI under RP 580 is one documented way of producing one. That distinction matters on the exam as well as at work, because RP 580 expects an RBI programme to work within the applicable codes and jurisdictional requirements, not around them. The standard also exempts retail facilities, oil or gas well drilling or servicing operations and normally unoccupied remote facilities, so a DJ Basin integrity engineer may find that some field sites fall outside PSM while the gas plant they feed does not.

Where an RBI result cannot set the interval

An API 580 candidate should know the places where regulation caps or replaces the RBI answer, and the Denver area has examples.

  • Breakout tanks. Pipelines that carry Colorado crude and products use breakout tanks, and 49 CFR 195.432(b) requires the atmospheric and low-pressure steel ones to be inspected to API 653 while barring its risk-based procedure for setting the internal inspection interval. PHMSA proposed in June 2026 to allow RBI intervals for breakout tanks within maximum limits, but that was a proposal, not a final rule.
  • Boilers and state-inspected vessels. Colorado's Division of Oil and Public Safety sets an inspection schedule by rule for the equipment its program covers, and an owner-user inspection organization's procedures must be acceptable to the Division's director. An RBI-based interval at such a site needs to sit within procedures the director has accepted.
  • The codes themselves. API 510, 570 and 653 each say how RBI may be used to set intervals and where their own limits still apply. The API 580 exam tests RP 580, but the course points out where the inspection codes take over, because candidates who hold those certificates are expected to know the join.

Consequence on the Front Range

Consequence of failure is where local knowledge changes an RBI result most. Suncor's refinery sits about six miles from downtown Denver, runs around the clock, sells nearly 95% of its products in Colorado and supplies about a third of the jet fuel used at Denver International Airport. Any RBI team assessing a site like that has to think about safety consequence for people inside and beyond the fence, environmental consequence for releases that reach soil or water, and business consequence when a regional supply depends on one refinery. RP 580 expects all three to be considered, and the exam asks how consequence is assessed and categorised rather than what any particular site has concluded.

A Weld County gas plant presents a different profile. Population density may be lower, but toxic consequence wherever hydrogen sulfide is present, flammable consequence from natural gas liquids and the business consequence of shutting in production upstream all feed the assessment. The course uses contrasts like these to make the consequence chapters concrete.

When the feed changes: reassessment

RP 580 treats an RBI assessment as something that must be revisited when the basis for it changes. Two Front Range facts show why. Suncor buys crude from the DJ Basin and also receives crude through its transmission system from Guernsey, Wyoming, so the crude slate a unit sees can shift with supply. And in Cheyenne, Wyoming, HollyFrontier, now HF Sinclair, ran the last crude through its refinery in August 2020, and the conversion to a renewable diesel unit processing refined soybean oil and animal fats was completed in 2021. A change on that scale would send any RBI team back to the start of its damage mechanism review.

The exam does not ask about either site. It asks what should trigger reassessment, such as process changes, new inspection results, failures, management of change and the passage of time, and how a team documents what it did. Learn those triggers as categories and you will recognise them however the question disguises them.

Data an RBI team needs from a Denver site

Data collection is one of the ten categories in the API 580 Body of Knowledge, and it is often where real programmes struggle. A refinery assembled from plants built in 1931, 1937 and the 1970s and bought in 2003 and 2005 is a useful thought experiment: equipment numbering, design records, past inspection reports and process data may have been kept to different conventions for decades before they had to sit in one assessment. Expect questions about what data an assessment needs, what happens when data is missing or uncertain, and how conservative assumptions should be documented.

In practice the data falls into a few groups, and the exam expects you to know why each one matters:

  • Design and construction data, such as materials, corrosion allowances, design pressures and temperatures, which set the starting point for any probability estimate.
  • Inspection history, including which techniques were used and how effective they were for the mechanisms in question, not just the dates of past inspections.
  • Process and operating data, from stream compositions to upsets and excursions, which decide which damage mechanisms are credible.
  • Consequence inputs, such as inventory, fluid properties, detection and isolation systems and what lies around the equipment.

A closed-book scenario from a gas plant amine unit

The API 580 exam is closed-book, so you need to reason from principles. Consider a scenario the course builds on.

  1. Picture a gas plant amine regenerator whose feed carries some hydrogen sulfide. It and its overhead system have been inspected externally and by spot thickness readings for years. Thinning is negligible, so the plan looks low risk.
  2. The team's damage mechanism review identifies amine stress corrosion cracking and wet H2S damage as credible. Spot thickness readings are poorly suited to detecting cracking, so the inspection history says little about the cracking mechanisms.
  3. Probability of failure for cracking should therefore reflect low inspection effectiveness, not the thinning record. Consequence reflects toxic and flammable release.
  4. The risk ranking rises, and the mitigation is a more effective technique for cracking at the next opportunity, documented with its reasoning.

Questions written around inspection effectiveness, the difference between thinning and cracking mechanisms, and the role of the damage mechanism review follow exactly this pattern.

Studying RP 580 for a closed-book paper

The 2026 Body of Knowledge bases the exam on API RP 580, 4th edition (August 2023) with Addendum 1 (March 2025), and lists ten knowledge categories: terms and definitions, risk assessment, the RBI programme, roles and qualifications, data collection, damage mechanisms, probability of failure, consequence of failure, risk management and documentation. The paper has 90 questions, 80 of them scored, in 3.25 hours. Read RP 580 through once for structure, then work category by category with practice questions, and save your hardest questions for the instructor.

Exam prep or an RBI study?

Passing API 580 shows that you understand RBI; it does not produce an assessment for your plant. If a Denver site needs the study itself, Atlantis also carries out remote RBI studies, and the two can run side by side: staff preparing for API 580 learn faster when their own equipment is being assessed.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from Denver

Owners, operators and consultancies can sponsor several staff at once, each studying at their own pace. Fees are quoted on request. Each candidate applies to API individually, and API does not currently require employment verification to recertify API 580, though candidates still renew on a three-year cycle.

faq.q: Can I take the API 580 exam from home in Denver?
faq.a: API's programme page says the API 580 exam can now be scheduled either at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring. Check the options and the technical requirements for your window when you apply, because they can change. The course itself is online and self-paced either way, with instructor Q&A, and there is no Atlantis classroom in Denver to attend.

faq.q: Does OSHA's PSM standard require RBI at the Commerce City refinery?
faq.a: No. The mechanical integrity element requires inspection and testing that follow recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices, at a frequency consistent with manufacturers' recommendations and good engineering practice. RBI under RP 580 is one way an owner can justify that frequency, but the standard does not name it. In Colorado, federal OSHA enforces PSM at private sites.

faq.q: Does DJ Basin production experience count toward API 580 eligibility?
faq.a: API asks for petrochemical industry experience alongside your education, and it decides what counts. Production and midstream work may qualify depending on what you did, so describe facilities, equipment and responsibilities accurately on the application. If you already hold a current API 510, 570 or 653 certificate, you qualify automatically and the question does not arise.

faq.q: Is API RP 581 on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: The 2026 Body of Knowledge lists one reference publication, API RP 580, 4th edition with Addendum 1. RP 581 is the quantitative method many programmes use, and RP 580 refers to quantitative approaches in general terms, but you are not expected to work RP 581 calculations. Study RP 581 for your job if your site uses it, not for this exam.

faq.q: Can a Colorado pipeline terminal use RBI to set breakout tank internal intervals?
faq.a: Not under the current federal rule. 49 CFR 195.432(b) requires atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks to be inspected to API 653 but excludes its risk-based procedure for internal intervals. PHMSA published a proposal in June 2026 that would allow RBI within maximum interval limits, but a proposal does not change the requirement until a final rule takes effect.

faq.q: Which edition of RP 580 should I study?
faq.a: The 4th edition, published in August 2023, with Addendum 1 from March 2025, which is what the 2026 Body of Knowledge names. API says the exam focuses on the most recent edition of RP 580, so if your company's procedures still quote the 3rd edition, learn the differences rather than relying on the older text.

faq.q: Will passing API 580 make me the RBI team leader at my plant?
faq.a: Not by itself. RP 580 describes a team with defined roles, including a leader, inspection and corrosion specialists, process and operations input and risk management responsibilities, and owners choose who fills each role based on experience. The certificate shows that you understand the methodology, which is a strong argument when you put yourself forward.

faq.q: I work on tank storage at a Commerce City terminal. Is API 580 relevant to me?
faq.a: It can be. RP 580 applies to fixed equipment generally, including atmospheric storage tanks, and many tank programmes use risk ranking to plan bottom and shell inspections. Two cautions apply: steel breakout tanks on pipelines cannot currently use API 653's risk-based internal interval, and for the API 653 tank inspector certificate itself you need the tank codes, not RP 580. See the API 653 course if tanks are your main work.

faq.q: How do I keep API 580 once I pass?
faq.a: The certification runs for three years. You can apply to recertify from 90 days before it expires, with a 90-day grace period that carries late fees, and API does not currently require employment verification for API 580 recertification. If the grace period passes, the certificate expires and you would need a new application and the full exam.
